key_insight: Directly estimating small energy-level differences can lower sampling costs by replacing the full Hamiltonian norm with a scale set by its derivative and the parameter shift.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make molecular forces, energy gradients, and response properties more accessible on early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
method: Combine time evolutions under the original and parameter-shifted Hamiltonians in one quantum circuit.
Use non-adaptive statistical sampling to reconstruct energy differences directly.
Jointly estimate energy eigenvalues and their differences to characterize the energy landscape.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations and resource estimates on prototypical systems, including the Fermi-Hubbard model, indicate reduced resource requirements without loss of precision.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based evidence; practical savings still depend on the cost and accuracy of implementing both Hamiltonian time evolutions.
paper_title: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation
